idiom_name: plain class or module-scoped state object with a subscriber list; Proxy traps only when interception is needed
implementation_notes: Nothing in the language binds a view to a model, so the local idiom is a plain object (a class instance or a module closure) that owns the screen state and the command methods plus an explicit subscribe(callback) list or a small event emitter; the view re-reads the model when notified. Proxy is the only reflective hook - it intercepts [[Get]]/[[Set]] and can turn property writes into notifications - but it adds a trap layer and does not reach nested objects without its own plumbing, so most code either calls a notify method explicitly or delegates reactivity to a framework (Vue's reactive state, a store library, React state). The framework-free model is directly unit-testable; only the binding half is framework code.
pitfalls: Passing a method as a callback loses its this binding unless it is bound or declared as a class field, so subscribers calling model.render fail at runtime.
In-place mutation is invisible to immutable-state frameworks (React state, Redux stores): the object must be replaced (or the framework setter used) for a re-render to be scheduled.
A Set of subscribers holds strong references - the unsubscribe function must run when a view unmounts or both the view and its DOM nodes leak.
Proxy interception is shallow: assigning to model.form.email does not trigger the model's set trap unless every nested object is proxied too or the write goes through a method.
